detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

# [CPU] Improve long-context MTP attention scheduling on AMX

## Purpose

Extend CPU attention's grouped-query (GQA) scheduling to eligible
causal multi-token requests, including MTP verification and short prefill. The
existing batch-level GQA fast path requires an all-q1 decode batch, so these
requests do not receive the same grouped scheduling. The scheduler evaluates
grouped query heads and split-KV work using each request's query length,
causality, and AMX geometry, then selects a plan through its cost model. This
applies with auto, FP8 E4M3, and FP8 E5M2 KV cache.

## Duplicate-work Check

PR [#46154](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46154) is related but not
a duplicate. It fixes generic mixed-batch GQA decode classification when
split-KV can divide a prefill request into one-token work items. This change
adds request-level eligibility based on causality, prefill state, and
verification query length, and uses it to enable AMX speculative multi-token
GQA scheduling with BF16 attention and FP8 KV.

Issue [#46131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46131), its comments,
open PRs referencing the issue, and open PRs matching CPU attention/GQA/spec
decode terms were checked. #46154 was the relevant overlap found.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -P -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_group_head_counts.py
.venv/bin/python -P -m pytest -s -v \
  tests/evals/mrcr/test_mrcr_correctness.py \
  --config-list-file="$MRCR_CONFIG_LIST"
```

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 128K \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# In another terminal:
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 100000 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 1 --num-warmups 1 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 1000
```

Serving uses BF16 TP1, batch size 1, and no prefix caching. The original
comparison also used auto KV with and without MTP3. The MRCR configs use the
existing 40-sample inputs and thresholds with three speculative tokens. Set
`MRCR_CONFIG_LIST` to the auto-KV or FP8-KV config list for each evaluation.

## Test Result

Serving used 100k input/1k output tokens with zero failures. Main
`6b24bd8e75a3` values are medians of three timed requests. Auto-KV branch
`65e9381658fe` values are also three-request medians; FP8 branch
`59b2f5f7b4` is one timed request after one warmup, built from the same source
state just before that commit. The FP8 fix leaves auto-KV scheduler selection
unchanged.

| Configuration | Main output tok/s | Branch output tok/s | Main TPOT (ms) | Branch TPOT (ms) | Main TTFT (s) | Branch TTFT (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No MTP, auto KV | 6.73 | 7.08 | 79.29 | 75.49 | 71.04 | 67.39 |
| MTP3, auto KV | 8.01 | 9.48 | 48.72 | 34.33 | 77.99 | 72.88 |
| MTP3, FP8 KV, post-fix | 8.62 | 9.36 | 37.25 | 27.57 | 80.73 | 81.20 |

The original FP8 branch run had **87.14 s TTFT**: its new AMX work
materializer also handled ordinary FP8 prefill. Routing FP8 batches without
eligible multi-token verification through the existing legacy materializer
reduced TTFT to **81.20 s**, within **0.58%** of main. FP8 MTP acceptance was
**98.7%** on the post-fix timed request (767/777 draft tokens). The generic
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` option maps to E4M3 in CPU attention on both arms.

- Original CPU attention and metadata tests: **1,637 passed, 1,154 skipped**.
  After the FP8 fallback, **24 focused cases passed** across AMX FP8 prefill,
  q=1, mixed MTP, builder masking, and forced VEC. FP8 E4M3/E5M2 attention
  with serving cache strides was within 0.3% of main at 98k context. Commit
  hooks passed.
- Original forced-VEC parity: **3/3 passed** with identical outputs. Native
  `amx_fp8` and ARM hardware were unavailable. The full kernel timing matrix
  was not repeated after the rebase.
- Qwen3.5-4B MTP3 MRCR: auto KV passed **40/40** on both main and branch with
  identical 2/4/8-needle scores (**0.9952 / 0.8444 / 0.7632**). Post-fix FP8
  KV completed **40/40** with scores **0.9952 / 0.9049 / 0.7055**, no lower
  than saved main (**0.9952 / 0.8581 / 0.7055**). Both fail the same n8 cutoff
  (**0.7055** versus **0.7100**); this is not an absolute FP8 MRCR pass.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for implementation, source review, build and test
planning, serving analysis, upstream overlap research, and drafting. The human
submitter will review every changed line and is responsible for understanding
and defending the complete branch.

+def _request_group(
+    query_len: int,
+    seq_len: int,
+    num_query_heads: int = 32,
+    num_kv_heads: int = NUM_KV_HEADS,
+    head_size: int = 64,
+    block_size: int = 32,
+    is_cross_attention: bool = False,
+    enable_kv_split: bool = True,
+    isa_hint: str | None = None,
+    cache_dtype: str = "auto",
+) -> int:
+    """Return the CPU scheduler's query-head group for one request."""
+    with patch("torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported", return_value=True):
+        builder = _build(
+            [num_query_heads],
+            block_size=block_size,
+            num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads,
+            head_size=head_size,
+            cache_dtype=cache_dtype,
+        )
+    if isa_hint is not None:
+        builder.isa = isa_hint
+    builder.is_cross_attention = is_cross_attention
+    common = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_reqs=1,
+        num_actual_tokens=query_len,
+        max_query_len=query_len,
+        max_seq_len=seq_len,
+        query_start_loc=torch.tensor([0, query_len], dtype=torch.int32),
+        seq_lens=torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32),
+        block_table_tensor=torch.zeros(
+            (1, (seq_len + block_size - 1) // block_size), dtype=torch.int32
+        ),
+        slot_mapping=torch.arange(query_len, dtype=torch.int64),
+        causal=True,
+    )
+    with patch(
+        "vllm.v1.attention.backends.cpu_attn.envs.VLLM_CPU_ATTN_SPLIT_KV",
+        enable_kv_split,
+    ):
+        metadata = builder.build(0, common).scheduler_metadata
+
+    # Workitem count is at byte 68; 48-byte items start at byte 192.
+    words = metadata.view(torch.int32)
+    workitem_count = words[68 // 4].item()
+    workitems = words[192 // 4 : 192 // 4 + workitem_count * 12].reshape(-1, 12)
+    groups = set(workitems[workitems[:, 0] == 0, 3].tolist())
+    assert len(groups) == 1
+    return groups.pop()

inline_comments.body: Meanwhile I think the `head_dim` check here is not required, AMX impls have check for it.
You can change the calculation of `min_split_kv_len` and avoid introduce a new threshold. The previous calculation is based on my intuition.
Maybe you can reserve sizes for these vector.

Since this PR is refactoring the scheduler, I think it's better to clarify the rules for GQA packing and build up a more concise schedule procedure. Otherwise more and more flags will make the code become hard to maintain. In my opinion:
- `max_num_q_per_iter % original_q_head_per_kv == 0`, regular cases, enable GQA by default, natural for prefill and decode requests.
- `max_num_q_per_iter % original_q_head_per_kv != 0 && max_num_q_per_iter >= original_q_head_per_kv`, enable GQA for decode and short prefill requests. The AMX tiles are not fully used, but GQA can reduce memory access for such memory bound cases.
- `max_num_q_per_iter < original_q_head_per_kv`, fallback to MHA. Such cases can enable GQA by split heads of a query to multiple iterations. But they should be very rare for AMX impls, which can support `max_num_q_per_iter = 32`.
Please leave some comments to explain the purpose.
Added AMX_FP8 to the packing rule and removed the scheduler's head-dimension check
Removed the separate adaptive threshold. Partition credit and split sizing now use one minimum: align_up(8 * max_num_q_per_iter, kv_alignment).
Added reservations for partition work/reduction vectors and final work/reduction/task vectors.

Consolidated eligibility into one rule. For causal multi-token AMX/AMX_FP8 requests, divisible groups pack queries up to the 32-row capacity; non-divisible groups pack only queries fitting one iteration. Oversized groups use MHA, and the existing q1 rule is preserved. Large q (e.g.: large prefill) still uses MHA as switching them to GQA introduces some regressions.
Added brief comments explaining packing eligibility, split credit, independently claimable iterations, and the span-count safeguards that retain GQA on ties.

I think we don't need to limit the GQA enabling just on AMX, other impls can config it based on their tiling sizes.

And I think GQA can be enabled for both of causal and non-casual reqs.

When `max_num_q_per_iter % original_q_head_per_kv == 0`, GQA can be always enabled no matter the query token  numbers. This is what FA3 did for varlen inputs. The performance of GQA and MQA should be close, their workitem number and memory access are similar in this case. Enable GQA by default can simplify the check condition.

Done. Divisible groups now always use GQA, and the subgroup/MHA search, packed-query flag and partition-credit discount are removed in favor of one split rule (split only tiles longer than a thread's KV share) and `min_split_kv_len = 16 * max_num_q_per_iter`.

Done. The group now depends only on each ISA's `max_num_q_per_iter` and the
query length.
